title: Policy compiler and schema checker for routing rules
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Refactor the routing policy engine to introduce a compile-time schema and a lightweight policy compiler that validates routing DSL configs for region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. Goal is to catch misconfigurations before deployment, provide clearer error messages to customers, and enable deterministic conflict resolution and precedence rules across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Background: Existing policy handling is dynamic and permissive which has led to subtle misrouting (incorrect region preference, unexpected tier overrides, and silent fallback to higher-cost variants). We need a validator that enforces: type correctness, mutually exclusive clauses, required fields for region and tier selectors, and explicit fallback chains for model variants. Additionally the compiler will emit an IR that the runtime can consume to speed up evaluation and to enable preflight simulation.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Implement a schema definition (JSON Schema + DSL-level extensions) that captures routing predicates, weightings, and fallback chains.
- Build a policy compiler that: (1) parses the DSL, (2) runs static checks (type checks, overlap/conflict detection, circular fallbacks), (3) emits a compact IR for the route evaluator.
- Add a dry-run simulator in Console that shows sample routing decisions for a given policy and request profile (latency/region/tier).
- Fail fast on invalid policy uploads with clear user-facing errors.
- Ensure backward compatibility: existing policies should be auto-migrated (with warnings) or rejected with migration guidance.
- Add unit and integration tests covering region preference, tier fallback, weighted routing, and edge cases (missing default fallback).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Strong typing vs flexibility: we choose a conservative schema that requires explicit defaults for fallbacks and tier priorities to avoid silent behavior; this increases friction for some simple users but reduces production incidents.
- Compiler complexity: prefer a minimal IR that encodes precedence and fallback tables rather than a full Turing-complete VM. This reduces audit surface and increases determinism.
- Migration strategy: auto-migrate simple, unambiguous rules; for ambiguous/conflicting policies surface a migration guide with examples and link to PR for manual changes.

Implementation plan:
1) Schema design RFC and examples (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Policy+Compiler+RFC) — target 1 week.
2) Parser + compiler library in Go (shared by hosted and Dedicated control planes). Emit tests and sample IR.
3) Integrate validator into API ingress: reject or warn on upload; wire up to Console to surface errors.
4) Simulator UI in Console and a CLI dry-run tool.
5) Migration job to detect patterns and propose fixes; ship with a feature flag.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for parser and static checks (edge cases around circular fallbacks).
- Staging rollout: validation-only mode for 2 weeks, then enable enforcement for new policies, then run migration for existing ones.
- Canary: 10% of policy updates routed through the new compiler for runtime compatibility checks.

Observability and metrics:
- Policy compilation errors per minute, categorised by error class.
- Number of auto-migrated policies and number of policies requiring manual fix.
- Router decision divergence metric during canary (percent of evaluations where new IR routes differently than old engine).

Acceptance test examples:
- Region selection: policy with preferred regions [us-west-2, eu-west-1] and secondary allowed regions should route to us-west-2 for requests originating from US; simulator must show that.
- Tier routing: strict tier routing where 'enterprise' traffic must not be routed to 'spot' instances.
- Fallback model variants: explicit fallback chain model.v1 -> model.v1-quant -> model.v2 and detection of cycles.

Links and artifacts:
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Policy+Compiler+RFC
- Design moodboard: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1policy-design
- Draft PR for parser prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/1284
- Simulator mockups: https://figma.com/file/abcdef/Policy-Simulator

Migration notes: Existing simple key-value policies will be auto-migrated by a small script (see migration PR). Policies using dynamic JS predicates will be flagged for manual review and replacement by whitelist predicates.

notes: Follow-up tasks: Add end-to-end test that compares runtime decisions for 50k synthetic requests between old and compiled IR.
Decision: require explicit 'default_fallback' for any policy that references non-stable model tags.
Risk: Customers using bespoke predicates may need migration help; schedule two office-hours sessions for partner teams.
Owner: Compiler library maintained in inference/pkg/policy/compiler. API integration in routing-service.
